utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, we left off yesterday where I asked you to look at two pieces of documents. I take it you thought about those documents overnight.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before I ask you whether you've changed your mind or not, I would like you to look at a clip of a video that was taken during your first meeting with General Mladic. And while that is being queued up, the video is already in. For the record, it's, I believe, Prosecution 21. And along with that, Your Honour, Mr. President, there was a transcript as Prosecution evidence 21/A. I did make excerpts, copies of that transcript for the convenience of everyone. And so I have them available, if the usher would like to distribute them while... And the videoclip, for everyone's convenience, will start on page of the transcript, the middle of the page of page 19, and at the top right-hand corner, it has L0092415 as the number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May copies be provided for the booths, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I should add we're being assisted by the Office of the Prosecution, and we're very delighted to have Ms. Janet Stewart assisting us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, did you have opportunity to review this video before?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen this video once before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have seen the video before?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it without the subtitles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you able to understand it?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood it fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And as I recall, I saw you in the video. You sort of stand up, you're taller than anybody else over there.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you had an opportunity to -- you were close enough to Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans and you were able to hear what he was saying at the time.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present during the entire meeting. I missed the beginning, let's say the first five minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, okay. But the clip that I showed showed you in the clip.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the clip that I showed had the relevant information that we were discussing yesterday. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you were able to hear and understand -- you were able to hear Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were able to understand his English as he was speaking to General Mladic. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you don't understand B/C/S or Serbo-Croatian, whatever the language was at the time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I understand that language very poorly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you understood -- you understood Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who is General Nikolai? He mentioned a General Nikolai in there.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Sarajevo. Let's say he was in charge of Sarajevo at that time. And Karremans was regularly in touch with him. And he was above the Tuzla line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And now, from the clip, it says that Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans notes that he had spoken with General Nikolai a couple of hours earlier. Do you recall hearing that part?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday I showed you those documents. And we're not clear whether they were received or not, but at least they note that they were faxed sometime around 3.40 in the afternoon that day. Somewhere around that period.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time of 1540 as written on the documents, 3.40, was on the 12th of July. That's one day later, if you look at the header. But if you mean that there has been contact by telephone between Nikolai and Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans, then, well, I presume that was the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you have no -- so would you like to recharacterise your testimony? Yesterday, you indicated, you were emphatic, you were certain, because of your memory, that it was the VRS that had insisted on the meeting. Now you see the video with Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans. You've also seen some documentation, one of which was generated by Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans, all indicating that it was Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans at the request of the folks in Sarajevo and the Bosnian government that he initiate contact with the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that's a misstatement of the facts, especially since he takes all these documents and other information which he says has been shown to the witness together. So it would be fair, especially when he talks about the document, to show it again to the witness because then he would realise that what he said about fax numbers and times, there appear several fax lines on that document, and only one is 3.40. So I would suggest that Mr. Karnavas be more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Since everybody has got that footage, you know, you may point to particular line or paragraph to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. But if I may, before I get to that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After leaving here yesterday, you took some documents with you to review. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you by any chance take the documents referring to the topic that we're discussing here today?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have those documents with me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But my question is did you have them last night with you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took them away. I read them, and I brought them here again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you had an opportunity to read them overnight before coming here today.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you watched the video again.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your testimony today that Karremans is incorrect in stating in the video that he was asked by General Nikolai and the government, meaning the BiH government, to make contact with the VRS with respect to the people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps if Mr. Karnavas could point to the part in the video where it says what he just stated, that General Nikolai requested Mr. Karremans to initiate a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would look at the transcript that was given to you, sir, and look at page -- at the bottom it says "page 19 of 78." In bold letters on the left side, it says "General Mladic." Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says in bold: "What do you want? You asked for a meeting. Speak up." Now, do you understand what he means by "You asked for a meeting"?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What do you understand it to mean?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans asked for a meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Not that General Mladic asked for the meeting. Right? You can't -- you don't get that impression from what General Mladic is saying?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So from that, can you conclude that at least from what we have here today it would appear that it was Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans who requested the meeting, and not General Mladic requesting the meeting?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the meeting was -- probably the subject of the meeting was raised a number of times, the fact that it was to be held. And it is quite possible that there has been a crossing by a request from us with a request from General Mladic, or someone, because it was not clear at the beginning of the meeting that General Mladic would be present there. So I assume that possibly there was a need on both sides for having a meeting. And that explains my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, was any part of my question with respect to your memory or was it with respect to what's on the paper here today and what's on the video?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm here as a witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm asking you from what you heard today and what's on the paper, is it not a fact that the only inevitable conclusion that you can draw, irrespective of your memory, is that Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans requested the meeting with the VRS and not the other way around?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the witness clearly answered the question in reference to his memory. And he is sticking to that. And if the counsel likes his answer not, the answer was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think, too, Mr. Karnavas, I fail to see how important in your question that who is requesting a meeting. Is that relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It will become relevant throughout the trial, Your Honour. At some point it will become relevant. And if the Court wishes to take judicial notice that the meeting was requested by the DutchBat with the VRS, I'll move on. If not, if we go -- as I go through this transcript, it will become very clear that it was the DutchBat that asked for the meeting irrespective of this gentleman's memory. And I intend to impeach him at this point unless he starts answering the questions correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no objection if these documents come in as documents and they speak for themselves. The witness was present there. And I think he testified yesterday that he was told by the Serb interpreter that the meeting was requested. And today he opened the possibility that there were requests from two sides. That's what he can state. The document is a different matter, and again it can come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think we have spent much time on that issue, and the positions of the two sides is quite clear to us. And at the same time, the witness has answered that question already. So I don't think there's a need to prolong the cross-examination on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, just so I understand, is this a request to move on, or are you giving a few more questions to ask on this topic? I don't mean to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope you could move on. I understand your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember at any rate that the two next meetings happened by order of General Mladic and that clear scheduling was dictated by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I totally agree with you, sir. I couldn't agree with you more on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But from reading this transcript and watching the video, it's very clear, at least in my opinion, and you can read it at your leisure, that General Nikolai spoke with Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans and requested a meeting to deal with the population that had gathered at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a statement by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was an invited response. There was no question posed to the witness. The witness decided to make a response, and invited a response on my part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, there's no need for you to argue with the witness. You are a professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, with the -- I take there was enough food there by the people that had gathered at Potocari that would sustain them for several days because they had brought with them provisions. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you certain?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you be so certain?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because an inventory had been made by a colleague of mine, and a plan was made. And I was present when the comment was given to that plan about the quantity of food and what the outlook was, a kind of staff meeting if you like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the outlook? How much food was available for everyone?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who is "everyone"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the question I posed was that the folks that had gathered to Potocari, that is, the folks from Srebrenica, had brought enough food for themselves to sustain themselves for several days. So now they're at Potocari, so would that statement be correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that statement is not correct. At most, some water they had. But in terms of food, hardly anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if that was the testimony of another witness, Mr. Mandzic, that would be totally incorrect because that was his assessment under oath. He had indicated that -- when I posed a question to him, that there was a humanitarian crisis and a lack of food, he said, oh, no, they had made provisions for several days for themselves. So in your opinion, that's an incorrect statement made by the Prosecution's witness, Mr. Mandzic?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I have seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, isn't it a fact that DutchBat had enough food for themselves and perhaps to assist the rest of the population for up to 24, maybe 48 hours, and no more after that? Or would you say less than that?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was the deadline, 48 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Before coming here today, were you made aware of the heavy battle that took place between the 28th division as they had left in the column with the VRS, and specifically with the Zvornik Brigade? Were you made aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were rumours that there was fighting, but no confirmation. We had no contact with military leaders of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But since then, I'm saying after you left, because as I understand it, you went to Tuzla, you were held there for a couple of hours by the Muslim army because they didn't trust you, not you in person but because you were a DutchBat, part of the UN that had failed to protect the enclave. And then it's my understanding you left. But since that period, were you ever made aware by the Prosecution or other official documents as to the heavy battle that went on between the VRS and the 28th Division as they were trying to get to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen official documents, but I read several books about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Had you been made aware of the official documents, of what exactly had transpired, the losses that were on the VRS, the Zvornik Brigade and others that were there, and the losses that were -- that had taken place by the 28th Division, might that have been of some assistance to you throughout my questioning as far as the strength, the numerical strength and the military capabilities of the 28th Division? Might that have been of some assistance in your assessment?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to avoid that. And I cannot give an unambiguous answer to this because memory has a special way of functioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is my last question. I just want to make sure you that understood my question. Probably it was my fault. It was inarticulately phrased. There were several questions yesterday posed to you about the 28th Division. And many of those questions were related to their numerical strength and military capability. And you were able to provide some answers, given your observations on the ground six months in that terrain. What I'm asking you today is had you been aware of the information that's available regarding what had happened with the Zvornik Brigade and the fighting, might that have been of some assistance in you evaluating your assessment as to the numerical and military capabilities of the 28th Division, vis-a-vis the VRS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: A couple of remarks. Yesterday the witness said repeatedly that he thought the strength of the armed forces inside the enclave was a thousand people. Now, today, he has asked about -- sort of giving an assessment, and he said that he was out of the area by that time. He only heard rumours. He read books about it. And it's very difficult for him to comment on battles which are not made clear when they happened, in what area they happened. I don't think that it would assist the Trial Chamber if this witness, who was not in the area at that time, was invited to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may briefly respond, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Briefly respond. Under normal circumstances, I might agree with the Prosecution. However, in this case, there is ample material within the Prosecution's Office that was made available to us regarding battles that took place between the 28th Division and the VRS, and specifically, the Zvornik Brigade, as they were leaving the area. It is obviously critical to us because the Bratunac Brigade was asked to assist on I believe it was the night of the 15th. So some men did go from the Bratunac Brigade to assist on a battle where heavy losses were sustained by the Zvornik Brigade. And in fact, the evidence will show that the people of Zvornik were quite concerned that Zvornik itself would be taken over by the 28th. What I was asking the gentleman was: Was if he had that information available to him would that assist him in his evaluation, in his assessment of the strength of the 28th because obviously that's information that wasn't known to him. He could say yes, or he could say no. So that's all -- because obviously he has a certain amount of information. So that was the purpose of asking the question. And I'm willing to live with whatever the answer is, and I'll end at that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the witness has already answered the question. He came here to tell us what he saw and what he did during that period. He himself did not witness the various fighting. He just got this information from some books as well as some rumours. After all, it's hearsay evidence. I don't know how far you could go, you know, in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My only question, what I was leading at, Your Honour, is had the Prosecution provided this information to him because in essence, they have put him on sort of as an expert, even though he's not titled as an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ask this question straight to the witness, whether the Prosecution provided such kind of documents or evidence to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know the answer is going to be no, Your Honour. So very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your opinion, you cannot give -- if you had all that information available that is in possession of the Prosecution, is it your opinion today that that would not assist you in any way in forming an opinion with respect to the strength of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the gentleman is thinking about the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me hear the answer from this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no idea of what is in the Prosecution's possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And I have no further questions. I want to thank you very much, Major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination from Defence team of Mr. Jokic? Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do have to say that my esteemed colleague here has left no stone unturned with this witness, but I may have five minutes worth of questioning. But certainly before the break, I'll be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Ms. Sinatra:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Major Boering. My name is Cynthia Sinatra, and I represent Dragan Jokic. First of all, I would like to thank you for your bravery on the front there in Srebrenica because you certainly stayed and protected the refugees against all odds, I believe, and only left at the last moment. You did leave July 13th with the first refugee bus out of Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 12th or the 13th. It was after the third meeting, that day. And what I recall is that it was the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I believe your prior testimony is it was the 13th, but if that's --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the day after the third meeting. It was the day of the third meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: We can certainly go and check what he says, but I would be extremely surprised if he had said he had left on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, the record will reflect whether he left on the 12th or 13th, and I'll be willing to continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement on February 10th, 1998, you confirm that each time you had a special mission, you wrote that your battalion commander was briefed, and that you wrote a report that was sent to UNPF sector North-East in Tuzla. You reviewed these reports before testifying today, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We certainly didn't report very often to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it would be quicker and easier for the witness if he was shown that portion of the witness statement since you're, in fact, quoting it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It depends, you know, how much content that Defence counsel would like to use. If you just ask a question on that statement, I don't think, you know, we have to put statement before the witness. If the Defence counsel will extensively use that document, the best way is to provide a copy to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to ask if there is an exhibit list that was to be provided by the Blagojevic team of the exhibits they used because I believe that statement was on the exhibit list used by the Blagojevic team, and then I could just refer to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm surprised to hear that you didn't get that list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I did not receive that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So the list does not include the statement that he made in February 1998. Is that what I recognise here? Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Boering -- Major Boering, do you have a copy of your statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have various statements. Which one are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one from February 10th, 1998.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, I've found it. Number 00583503.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. The third paragraph, you say the battalion commander was always briefed after each mission, and I would prepare a report to this effect.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have those reports that you prepared during that time, July 8 through July 12th in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't draw up any reports in that period, not on paper. I didn't. It was all done orally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The paperwork was done by Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to confirm, you did state that the VRS army did seize some DutchBat equipment, APCs, uniforms, et cetera, during the initial takeover of the observation post. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. And you know for a fact that sometime during the movement of the refugees, those APCs, helmets and uniforms were used to disguise the VRS soldiers. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw uniforms, not APCs or helmets when the refugees were taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not aware of an APC being seized by the VRS army?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, but at a different point in time. We heard and saw the vehicles at a different point in time. I believe that that was at the time of the first or perhaps the second meeting at Fontana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was July 11th, then, that this APC may have been seized?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- no, no, no, it happened earlier, when the observation posts were taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Since you were the liaison officer between DutchBat, the civilians, the VRS, and the BiH army, you were advised about different intercepts and communications coming in and out of the posts, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the word "posts."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming in and out of your military compound, your command.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, I don't understand the question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- you were aware of communications coming in and out with various radio communications between the Bosnian army, the VRS army, and possibly with UN forces somewhere else in the area.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that in any case, from the PTT building, there were contacts, possibilities of liaison for the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that the Bosnian army had a thick blanket of radio intercept spots, locations, all around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the DutchBat system, DutchBat command post centre there in Potocari, did it have a radio intercept location in there to intercept the Bosnian army and the VRS army radio communications?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in so far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you wouldn't be able to give me a name of some officer or some other Dutch military person that was working in that area with radio intercepts?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we didn't have such a person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then you, of course, would not know anything about the American NSA satellite photographs of the area or NSA intercepts of the area during that time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing was known about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back to your statement with regard to a meeting -- the last meeting that you had with Karremans and Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't see without my glasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would please turn to the page that's marked 00583511, last paragraph, you stated: "We returned to Potocari between 1100 and 1200 hours. I discussed the contents and decisions of the meeting with Colonel Karremans. It seemed that he had forgotten about the execution of the plan and the evacuation and supply of fuel for the transportation of refugees. I noted that Karremans had trouble remembering details of our meeting with the Serbs. I don't think he made extensive notes at the meetings either. He looked stressed at that point, just as I myself might have looked." Let me ask you, did Karremans seem a bit incapacitated at the time, after this meeting? Let me rephrase my question. I retract that one. If Karremans had immediately and timely set up the logistics for the UN escorts of the refugees, don't you think that this tragedy may have been prevented?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he was in a position to be able to set this up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, of course, he did commit to a joint venture with the VRS in the meeting where he agreed that they would provide the buses and the trucks to evacuate the refugees, and he would supply the fuel. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, with regard to fuel he was to make inquiries. And as far as I can remember, there was some unclarity with regard to the vehicles and General Mladic indicated that he was willing to organise that himself, and we just the fuel. That's my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the truth is from the videotape of Karremans just a moment ago, he stated they had no fuel, so he couldn't have honoured his agreement with Mladic, could he?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would ask higher up whether they could organise that from Zagreb or Sarajevo. That was General Mladic's request, and certainly not from Potocari. And that is why it was going to take some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He asked the higher-ups in Zagreb and Sarajevo for air cover also, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: What point of time are you referring?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that the Serbs were overtaking the Srebrenica enclave, July 11th, I believe.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, requests were submitted. I wasn't present myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the air cover came too little, too late, too, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: You might characterise it like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, if we hadn't had a combination of too little, too late air cover, too little, too late, fuel, Sarajevo withdrawing Naser Oric, the protector of the Muslims in the area, these casualties might have been prevented. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, I don't think this is a good form of question because you are asking the witness to speculate. Put your question another way. Don't put hypothetical questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I was just going to ask if he formed an opinion. He was there, he was present during all of these meetings, all of the distress calls, all of the SOS's, he's familiar with the withdrawal of Naser Oric at the last moment. I believe the witness could answer if he has an opinion, not from speculation, but the opinion he formed from being present at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What we are going to hear is the fact, not the opinion of this witness. This witness came here not as an expert witness, just as a fact witness. Withdraw your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I withdraw the question. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Boering, did you feel deserted and abandoned at the time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By UNPROFOR, by the BH army, by everyone around you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps also by VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I pass the witness, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any redirect? Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, at this moment, are there any documents to tender? From the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, there are, Mr. President. And I believe we gave a list already to Your Honours and the Defence. And on that list, it's called "Exhibit for Pieter Boering," the ones that had already been introduced via witness Jean-Rene Ruez are indicated. And the rest we would suggest should be tendered at this point with the only exception of P43, because that video still has not been used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So the documents listed on that list are admitted into evidence, except Document P/23. Are there any documents to tender at this moment from the Defence team? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we did provide a list as was requested by you yesterday. And the numbers are D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, and D6. And it has a description of all these documents. We are not tendering the statements given by the major in light of your ruling a couple of days ago. That's it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have no objections to the admission of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm asking if you have any documents to tender.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, we have no documents to tender, but we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any objections from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those documents D1 to D6 are admitted into the evidence as the Defence evidence. Thank you very much, Witness, for coming to the Tribunal to give your evidence. We wish you good luck in your future.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we also thank the interpreter who is sitting there all the time to assist us. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's about ten minutes left. Shall we have an early break and start earlier? I see everybody is nodding. So we will resume at 10 minutes to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now, before we have the next witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I could go into private session for a very brief comment and request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration according to the paper the usher is showing to you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Davis, your witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Davis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please state your name.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: My name is Paul Groenewegen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you spell your last name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: G-r-o-e-n-e-w-e-g-e-n.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Groenewegen, can you please tell us what your current affiliation is with the Dutch army.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: My rank is corporal first class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak into the microphone for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you still employed by the army, Mr. Groenewegen?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how are you currently employed?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: At this moment, I'm awaiting to leave service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not currently in active service?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's my understanding that you're in some sort of transition period, transitioning out of the army?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me when you enlisted or began your service with the Dutch military?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That was in January 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your age at the time?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: 17 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you served continuously with the Dutch army from January 1994 until now?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you told us that you're a corporal at the present time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your rank when you first enlisted?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Soldier, private.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of your military service, did you ever serve in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: In Potocari, Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the dates of your tour of duty in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: From January until July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that your only tour of duty in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, from November 1999 until May 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: In Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I think you're aware, we're going to focus today on the period that you spent in Bosnia in 1995. We've heard from Major Boering that there were two companies of the Dutch battalion assigned to the Srebrenica enclave. I think they were Bravo and Charlie to my recollection. Does that sound right to you?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which of these companies were you assigned?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The Charlie company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was Charlie company based?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: In Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's in the northern part of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time when you arrived in Srebrenica in January of 1995, you held the rank of private?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for us your general duties during the first six months of 1995, from January through June approximately of 1995.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Mainly we patrolled the area and the borders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You should be seeing on your screen in a moment a map of the Srebrenica enclave that has previously been admitted into evidence as Exhibit 20.1. Was your -- the patrols that you describe, were they performed from the Potocari compound?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Also, but mainly from the OPs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you served both from the compound and from the OPs?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- I apologise. Can you explain if there was some rotation of duty.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: It was customary to spend one week at the compound, followed by two weeks at one OP, then one week at the compound, and two weeks at another OP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the exhibit that you should have on the screen before you, can you indicate to the Trial Chamber -- can you identify where -- whether there were certain OPs that you were assigned to?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: In my case, it was OP Mike, OP November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your observations during your time at the OPs, was there to some degree a BiH army military presence inside the enclave?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of -- well, we usually refer to the Bosnian Serb army as the VRS, just for clarification. I may use that term. I believe you usually use the term BSA. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'll understand if I say VRS, I'm referring to what you call the BSA. Were you aware also of BSA positions outside the borders of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you mentioned earlier that part of your duties were to perform border patrols.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the border patrols?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: To see whether there were no conflicts between the two warring parties and whether -- to see whether the truce was respected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the first few months of your assignment, did you -- beginning in January 1995, did you witness any military activity between the two sides?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you witnessed.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Shootings back and forth, sometimes an explosion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those first few months, did the OPs to which you were assigned ever come under fire from either side?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to the first week of July 1995. Can you tell me where you were assigned during that first week of July.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I was at OP Mike at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that part of a regular rotation?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you recall, approximately when did that rotation begin?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: About two weeks prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that particular rotation at OP Mike, did you and the other soldiers who were there with you have any interaction with BSA forces in their nearby positions?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what kind of interaction you had.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The shooting of OPs with small calibre, large calibre, and mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me approximately what day this firing began.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to be certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was in the first week of July?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see the BSA soldiers from your position?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there ever any communication between you or the other soldiers at the OP and the BSA soldiers in their nearby positions?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was some firing on the OP during that first week of July. Were you aware whether this was occurring at any other OPs at the time?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: As a result of internal messages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at some point return to the base at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: In July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that returning to the base part of your regular rotation?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 10th of July when you returned to the base at Potocari, what was the mood of the DutchBat soldiers when you returned?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Tense, but not worried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say it was tense?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Everybody expected something to happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the firing on the OPs?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you spent the remainder of the day on the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Cleaning up our equipment and preparing for subsequent activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you preparing for subsequent activities?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: By going to our station of orders and receiving the next orders there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any particular orders on the night of the 10th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to the 11th of July and ask you how the situation changed in Potocari on July 11th.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The night between the 10th and the 11th of July, we slept in the bunker. And we were woken up early in order to cater for the first refugees coming in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you slept in the bunker. Was that an ordinary procedure, or was that due to the firing on the OPs?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Because of the firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the morning of July 11th, you were awakened early to -- I believe you said to cater to the first refugees coming in. Can you tell me about the arrival of the refugees in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: At that moment, little numbers of refugees started to trickle in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what time was that, that they began to trickle in, as you recall?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: They had been on their way before we had been woken up. So I can't really tell you when things started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from which direction were the refugees arriving?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: From the direction of the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's in the south. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for me the physical, and based on your observations, the emotional condition of the refugees.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: They arrived very exhausted and full of fear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they primarily on foot or were they being transported some other way?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The majority did. Others had been brought to the base by UN vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were your responsibilities or assignments with respect to the refugees?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: To ensure that people wouldn't get lost or wouldn't take roads that weren't meant for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have particular orders with respect to where to direct the refugees?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: We were to direct them towards the base where at the time, there was still space.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the space run out at the base at some point?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes, quite soon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The stream of refugees increased, and they gathered in the area around the base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the evening of the 11th, can you estimate approximately how many refugees were in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Thousands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was inside the UN Compound and outside the compound?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they -- had they taken shelter outside the compound?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: People tried to find shelter in the factories and the houses that were left empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there also people outside on the roads?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Most people had to stay outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the night between the 11th and the 12th of July, did you return to the bunker to sleep?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, we slept outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Amongst the refugees?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: In a free space that we had created for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sleep through the night?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No. We didn't get the opportunity. An hour or two at the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were sleeping in shifts. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you would be called upon to relieve other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were not asleep during that night, what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Assist people who required help or asked for assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what the scene was like during the night between the 11th and the 12th, what you heard, what you saw.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Mothers and children, elderly men, having not enough food, a few blankets at the most. And it was cold during the night, so these were not the right conditions for people to sleep outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to the 12th of July, 1995. You mentioned that you spent the night outside among the crowd. Did you remain there with the refugees on the morning of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at some point on the 12th, did you see BSA forces approaching Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you witnessed.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Groups of heavily armed infantry who were moving from the road in the direction of OP Papa towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. They were moving in the direction of OP Papa or they were coming from the direction of OP Papa?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: They came from the direction of OP Papa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's from the north?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the direction of Bratunac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were groups of heavily armed infantry. Did you notice that the soldiers arrived in stages or in groups?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I hesitate to object. I haven't been objecting to the leading nature of the questions. I would appreciate if she would not lead the witness. She can rephrase the question. I know it's a little more difficult to do it that way, but I would prefer the classic, nonleading approach now that we're into this area. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. With the last question, I agree with you. Ms. Davis, you have to put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the first soldiers that you saw arriving in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: They were not dressed as an ordinary army. It was a gathering of all sorts of camouflage, and the same goes for the arms they were carrying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the soldiers were arriving, could you see or hear any activity in the hills surrounding the village?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: At the same time as the soldiers came in along the road, we noticed that troops were also coming in through the hills. And we heard shelling explosions, and we saw houses catching fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you witness additional BSA troops arriving at a later point?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: After the groups of soldiers, the infantry had come in. About 20 or 30 minutes later, other groups came in which appeared to be press to us, cameras, sound recordings, and what appeared to be officers to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this second group that you describe as containing members, camera crews, and what appeared to you to be officers, did they appear to be acting in coordination with the group that had arrived previously?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: It looked like that very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the refugees, if you saw that, when the soldiers arrived?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Initially, most people were afraid and tried to move the other way again, towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the crowd of refugees moved towards the southern part of the village?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, they wanted to do it, but finally they were spoken to so that they would stay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to take us to a little bit later in the day, and I'd like to show you a very short videoclip. And as it rolls, if you could tell us what you're seeing in the video and what's going on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the buffer zone we had created for ourselves between the refugees you see over there and the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in this area that we're seeing on the video at the time?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether you were able to identify yourself, but you believe that you're one of the soldiers there in the blue helmets?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No doubt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain in that general area for most of the day on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that it was a buffer zone that you had created. Can you explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: When we arrived in the area, it was our duty to keep the two parties in the conflict separated. And therefore, that day, too, we tried to maintain a free area between the refugees and the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I noticed in the video that there was some tape strung in front of the crowd of refugees. What was the purpose of that tape?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: To retain the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me just by general description where approximately in the Potocari area this videoclip takes place.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: It's immediately outside the area of the compound in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be showing you in a little while an aerial, and you'll have an opportunity at that time to point it out on that. Corporal, did you become aware at some point on the 12th that refugees were going to be transported out of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes, we heard that in advance and saw the buses coming in afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe -- and did the transportation of refugees out of Potocari at some point begin?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes. The first people to go there were those who wanted to get into the buses on their own account. The people who didn't want to get in kind of withdrew into the background and were forced afterwards to get into the buses still.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you witnessed people being forced to get on to the buses?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw with respect to people going unwillingly to the buses?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Initially, there was only shouting and people were being called names. And if they still didn't want to get in, then violence was used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about shouting, calling names and violence being used to take people forcibly to the buses, can you tell me whether it was Dutch soldiers or Serb soldiers who were doing these things?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of the refugees were being taken to buses as you were in this area on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: All the people in the area at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was women and children and men?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a predominance of women and children, or were there equal numbers of men being taken to the buses?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: It struck us almost immediately that it was almost mainly women, children, and elderly men. We understood that the younger men were being kept behind in the hills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "being kept behind in the hills," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: We talked to some people among the population, and they were convinced that it was better for them to stay behind and fight, rather than to go along willingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there, in the crowd of refugees at Potocari, some younger men?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those men boarding the same buses as the women were?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, the men were selected from the large crowd and gathered in an empty house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to me what you saw with respect to men being separated from the crowd.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Most of the younger men were taken out of the crowd rather aggressively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: By Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the case that a single soldier would select a man out of the crowd, or were more soldiers involved?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Ms. Davis will need to ask nonleading questions, who, what, where, why, how, and explain. She can simply explain what he saw and he can explain what he saw. I don't want to interrupt, but I believe she is trying to lead the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think this question is just at the border. But anyway, Ms. Davis, try to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how the Serb soldiers would remove a man from the crowd or select a man from the crowd.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: It was done in many different ways. A single soldier removing a single man or a single soldier picking out groups, or groups of soldiers picking out groups of people. And finally, they were all gathered in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were speaking earlier about the transportation process, people being transported on buses. Did that process continue through the day on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Until in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it continue through the night?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night on the 12th, the night between the 12th and the 13th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Outside in the -- on the same lawn as where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the scene that night of the 12th in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The people who were still there at that time were mainly people who did not want to get on to the bus and wanted to stay. So the mood was fearful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the transportation of refugees continue on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes. Early in the morning, new buses came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were your duties on the 13th with respect to the refugees?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Possibly to see to it that everything went smoothly, to limit the aggression on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you an aerial of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Davis, for the sake of the record, whenever you use an exhibit, please indicate to us the number of that exhibit on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's number 50, Exhibit 50. Premarked as 50, I should say. And if we could have the aerial placed on the ELMO by the usher, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Groenewegen, if you can take a look at the aerial --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Is there a pointer there that the witness could use?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just indicate -- first, let me ask you if you recognise the landmarks that are visible there on the aerial of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Certainly. This is the area right outside the Potocari base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate with the pointer the general area where you were -- where you spent your day on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: It was in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you spend most of your day there, or did you move around?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Certainly. We walked up and down a bit here and there in order to try and stop people who tried to move far away from the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there at that point on the 13th a line similar to what there had been on the 12th, of where the refugees were being kept?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you -- were your duties similar to what they had been on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the area that you indicated on the aerial where you spent most of the day on the 13th, can you tell me what you witnessed with respect to the refugees.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: At a given moment, I and a group of other soldiers were sent from the road into the lawn to keep a watch over that area as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you there and ask you, you mentioned earlier in your testimony that you had seen men separated from the crowd and taken to a house. Does the house that you were referring to appear on the aerial?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show me using the pointer where the house is. And I am going to have you mark this aerial a little bit later on.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The house where -- to which I saw refugees taken was this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I'm not seeing the pointer on my screen. I don't know if the Trial Chamber is seeing that. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to the separations that you had described, was that a process that you saw on the 13th as well?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that men would be separated from the crowd and taken to a house. Could you see into the house?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: From some spots, I could, because one wall had disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I'd like to play a short videoclip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While it's rolling, if you could tell me whether you recognise the house that you're describing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the house that you were describing on the video?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Not quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Davis, what's the number of that --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. That is P48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: We can play it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take a look?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this area look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do any of those houses look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they located near the area where you were standing on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any one of those houses as the house where you saw Muslim men being taken or separated from the crowd?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: On the video, I could not see the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we could... How many men would you estimate that you saw separated and taken to the house that you were describing during the day?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I would have to make a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you make a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: A few hundred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were all of those few hundred men held in the house at the same time?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No. As soon as the house was full, they were taken to a bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The buses drove off in the same direction as the ones into which the buses with the women and children had disappeared. And as soon as the house was full again, the same was repeated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the men on the same buses as the women, or were these separate buses?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: There were other buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little bit earlier, you mentioned that the line of soldiers was extended beyond the road, I believe. At some point, you had orders.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to me what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: We were sent into the side field in order to keep watch over that area so that -- and to send people back who wandered too far off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you in the line?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I was the furthest removed from the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking again at the Exhibit P50, which should still be on the ELMO for you, if -- am I correct that the road that we see going north/south in the middle of the video is the main -- I'm sorry, in the middle of the aerial is the main north/south road through Potocari?
